where_is.detail: letter.php cache entry (address= in the key; letter body)
where_is.recovery: Chrome HTTP cache, block-file format. The key, which has a partitioned-cache prefix, carries the deposit address, 'session' + the full order ID (whose first 13 hex digits are the creation time) and the mode; the gzip body is the letter text with the full order ID, the deposit and destination addresses, the fee percentage, the server-local date block and the 48-hour validity paragraph. Match the letter.php URL as a substring of the key.
where_is.caveat: The key is longer than the 160-byte key field of one 256-byte block, so the entry spans two blocks; a viewer that shows one block cuts the key after the 13-hex creation-time prefix, before the rest of the ID and the mode parameter.

interpret.subject: uniqid_order_id
interpret.derivation: PHP uniqid(prefix, true) with the literal prefix 'session' internally (session<13 hex><digit>.<8 digits>); the UI strips the prefix. The first 8 hex characters are the unix seconds of order creation, the next 5 the microseconds, then a decimal entropy suffix (one digit, a point, eight digits). The letter.php cache key carries 'session' + the full ID, so the creation time can be read from the cache key alone (its first 13 hex digits); the full ID is also in the cached letter body.
